At least according to a quick naive search with Claude, despite the massive corpus of proofs our AI agents have generated there is a surprisingly little custom tactics and proof automation - I asked it to look at Tau Ceti, Lean Pool, the 1m unit distance proof, and my auto-formalization projects. Does anyone have a good intuition whether this is a missed opportunity (I am sure with steering, AI can write tactics just fine), or the math doesn't lend itself to more tactics writing.

reminds me of this essay for programming - https://bcantrill.dtrace.org/2026/04/12/the-peril-of-laziness-lost/ AI is not lazy enough to seek clever solutions.

There are likely good training/reward mechanism, specialist data training and such nuance here.

You almost always want to avoid meta code (in principle the AI could have been redundantly remaking/modding mathlib tactics this whole time, in some ways).

Perhaps their specialist curated data angle is for the math and they are not thinking of meta programming in that specialist additive sense. Overall though, I have seen some early signs of it trying meta programming more.

And I do think that there is no reason to think meta code will not be used by AI (eventually), as Leo said in his postmortem, me in my blog, countless others etc..it makes no sense to think otherwise IMO.

One of the issues with all of that, is in meta-programming there are indeed known ways to skirt stuff to remain flexible for general use.

Sure comparator will catch it, but that's not a good feedback loop.

Makes sense, but I guess I am not interested as much is "why is it not using meta programming", but if we want to approach "mathlib-level quality" do we believe this is an area that we should push for more usage more directly, as we believe it will give us some of the wanted outcomes - fewer loc, more readable proofs, faster checking(?). You make a good point that it can also push AI towards the more dangerous parts of lean bugwise.

I believe this is indeed going to be a huge part of the future, if AI-math utopia mega projects ( that can even ever finish building) are to be achieved.

I further think based on Leo's comments on LinkedIn and etc, my blog and all others (sorry I could do a full list and tag many here but it would be hefty) and threads etc, the recent debacle is somehow demonstrating a tight delta between old and new model -- in the specialist realm of TT/TCS knowledge (one leading theory is @Ramana Kumar had less advanced AI but this expert knowledge to compensate).

Edit: Sent DM with context on that.

That tells me they are doing more and more of this expert directional training stuff.

As the data gets poisoned , the progress has to slow naturally , the question is how much.

Obviously pristine Internet provides the most etc.

This slop has been spread way faster than many thought perhaps , and with the “% of novel info “ density getting lower , you need exponentially more computation to extract any such nugget . And in fact you can make yourself worse if not careful.
In terms of what we can do from our side, I have been trying a lot to get it to tactic better. But its hard, all you can use is context and such, technically weights are frozen.
I use hundreds of new tactics in catcrypt.

Bas Spitters said:

I use hundreds of new tactics in catcrypt.

Do have any visibility as to level of redundancy / "reinventing the wheel" wrt to the Mathlib tactic-reachable space? Probably would be hard though tbh

(Disclaimer: I have tried a few times to measure something like this though, to little avail)
Most of them are custom tactics for program verification etc. I'll have a closer look at math-lib related tactics. I believe a couple of new tactics for reasoning about concrete matrices fx.

Bas Spitters said:

Most of them are custom tactics for program verification etc. I'll have a closer look at math-lib related tactics. I believe a couple of new tactics for reasoning about concrete matrices fx.

Yea no worries , as you surmised mine is (unfortunately?) maths lmao. Say that since yours seems to be going better in that regard (but also maybe meta code is more relevant in general and less risky).

Unless you fine-tune or retrain the AI, the base model isn't going to intuitively know about your tactics. You can use skills or add the tactics to the memory for the model, but this may not work as well.

I think a workflow of creating the tactics with a bunch of examples, and then fine-tuning the LLM on them could potentially improve things. Although, this might depend on having access to fine-tuning infrastructure on stronger model.
